name: Behavior-Preserving Refactoring
summary: Behavior-preserving frontend refactoring orchestration with evidence, risk classification, diff budgets, step verification, rollback, and proof reporting.
description: Use when restructuring existing frontend code while preserving observable behavior, including responsibility extraction, module movement, conditional simplification, API cleanup, or data organization. Do not use for new feature behavior, behavior-changing bug fixes, dependency or framework migrations, or proven dead-code cleanup.

boundaryWorkflows: Use dead-code cleanup for proven unused code, exports, styles, routes, fixtures, or dependencies.
Use TDD when adding new observable behavior or fixing a behavior-changing defect.
Use debugging first when the failure cause is unknown.
Use validation repair for understood lint, typecheck, test, or build failures that predate the refactoring step.
Use code review for merge-readiness review rather than structure-changing execution.
Use migration or architecture planning for dependency, framework, router, state-library, or platform replacements.
